Game is a great introduction into jumping territory. Instead of dumping all the mechanics on the player at once, the game introduces them gradually, one by one. Main story route introduces collectibles which do not matter and only purpose (outside of achievements little bit) is to make the player dip into higher difficulty jumps. 

Once you finish the game (main storyline eta 6 hours), you are either satisfied or you want more jumping levels and this game provides that. 

Pros:
+ For the main storyline, levels are made short to be less frustrating, which worked
+ Great music/sfx
+ Pixel art for level design is a great choice, considering you have less distraction in the level while enough orientation where everything is
+ Cute story, good enough to enjoy it while also not really necessary to focus on
+ Game has great level of key imputs, feeling like most of the mistakes player makes are on him
+ Developers gave some generous hitboxes

Cons:
- Like i get it, but i really hated cycles, where you have to estimate them from start and hopefully hit them in the middle of room.
- In later levels i got somewhat confused of the path i need to take. In some cases i had to search up the solution. Can be called skill issue and someone finds them as a puzzle to solve, but i would love some indicators instead.


Final result for completing all achievements:
57 hours and ~16 000 deaths. Am i Proud of it? Yes, for my first jumping genre game outside of Hollow Knigh/Silksong i think i did well and i enjoyed every moment.

Beautiful story-telling wrapped in a challenging game.

I very much appreciated the themes of self-acceptance, depression, perseverance, and identity in this game. The game doesn't present these topics too on the nose, nor too vaguely. I liked the challenging and precise platforming, although I don't think I will go back to get all collectibles as I know the game will only get harder in the post-game and I think I've reached my skill ceiling.

I liked the pixel art that makes for beautiful environments and very distinct levels, each with their unique gimmicks and puzzles to complete. The characters are likeable and mostly shine in their full artwork. I especially love the details in Celeste's design, when you obtain the second dash, turning you from pink to blue. The ending of the game feels very gratifying and does not punish the player with the most atrocious platforming made to torture you. The controls are smooth and snappy, best experienced with a controller.

Overall a very enjoyable experience with themes I much appreciated.

When I played this game for the first time, I wasn't expecting much. I knew it wasn't an easy platformer, but it was way harder than I expected. Because of that, I dropped the game at chapter 4 in 2023 and haven't thought about it since.

Three years later, I decided to look through my Steam library and found this game abandoned in the dust. I decided to try it again from the very beginning, and oh man... it's freaking amazing.

I can't praise enough how fluid the movement feels, with the camera naturally tracking your character. It's also not as punishing as games like Getting Over It or Jump King, as it features checkpoints and lets you practice any room you want at your own pace. You can also save your progress anytime you want and come back to it whenever you feel like it.

The story is also amazing and very relatable. Our main protagonist, Mabeline, struggles with laziness and wants to prove to herself that she can accomplish anything she desires, even something as crazy as climbing to the top of a mountain. She goes through natural character development and proves to us players that if we truly desire something, we can achieve it. 

If you love challenging games that make you feel devastated after countless failures, but absolutely amazing after you accomplish your goal, this is the perfect game. I will keep playing to get 100% achievement completion, as it's truly worth it.

Got this game for free on Epic, decided to buy it here cuz fuck epic but also this game deserves the money.

Insanely mechanically tight, it will put your keyboard / controller's buttons (especially the fucking Dpad) under severe scrutiny, especially in the last few challenges. I'd rather not spoil anything tough, you wanna experience every level and feature blind.

The story is neat. I remember really liking it when I first played it, now I'm kinda meh on it, but that's probably just cuz of the state of mind I'm in. It's an analogy for overcoming hardships (not some tranny shit as "the tolerant and inclusive" communities on the internet would have you believe)

However, I think it's beyond retarded to give a game with this theme a fucking practice mode. Wtf was the dev thinking with that one I have no idea. Do not touch it, the intended experience is to figure every room out or die trying, not getting a fucking cheatmode to stroll through and find every secret without a hitch.

There are very very few instances of the game cheating, I don't recall them all anymore, but the most recent one is, for instance, a certain block falling faster than others when it fucking shouldn't in the hardest level (excluding the DLC). These are very rare, but they will piss you the fuck off since they have a major impact.

I guess I should say that I have not finished Farewell yet, I just finished [i] everything else [/i] though and now I'm taking a fucking break. 

Overall this game is a 9/10, and very close to a 9.5 at that. Mechanically tighter than any mario game, almost as consistent as fucking chess, despite being quite simple in the amount of mechanics the game provides. It milks them to the maximum and expects you to master them all.

Also the soundtrack is great, a shame [spoiler] the C sides [/spoiler] do not have a unique variation of the track, and also Golden Ridge Remix sucks ass.
